content.thinking:
I'm going through the four claims one by one against the record. The first is that an alarm fired for the io-shop service while no shop user saw a problem, and the header line supports that. The second is that the shop's own measurements show no errors matching the alarm, with the record not saying why it fired. The third is that since the alarm was disproven, there was no failure to measure a disruption length for. The last is that the business lost nothing and no customers were affected.

I'm checking the last two claims: that nobody on call was paged because no on-call incident was linked, and that nothing needed fixing beyond disproving the alarm. Both match the record, so I'm treating them as supported.

supported.quote: An error alarm for the io-shop service went off, but nobody using the shop saw anything wrong.
rows: Nobody using the shop saw anything wrong; an error-rate alarm fired with no matching errors

supported.quote: The shop service's own measurements showed no errors to match the alarm, and the record does not show why the alarm went off.
rows: Summary: An error alarm for the shop service went off even though the service's own measurements showed nothing wrong

supported.quote: Because the alarm was disproven, there was no failure and so no length of disruption to report.
rows: Nothing broke: the alarm was disproven, so there was no failure to time.

supported.quote: The business lost nothing and no customers were affected.
rows: Impact: none - the alarm was disproven
Nobody using the shop saw anything wrong

supported.quote: Nobody on call was paged, since no on-call incident was linked to this one.
rows: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.
What went wrong: The alert was not linked to an on-call incident

supported.quote: Nothing needed to be done to resolve it beyond disproving the alarm.
rows: Resolution: Nothing needed doing: the alarm was disproven.
